comparisons.label: Panel/display path off
comparisons.note: Existing brightness; touch disabled in both runs; includes changes in scanout/rendering.

comparisons.label: Touch delivery disabled
comparisons.note: Software delivery only; does not establish controller hardware sleep or gesture wake.

comparisons.label: Deeper CPU idle enabled
comparisons.note: Only original enabled states are toggled; no physical SoC rail proof.

comparisons.label: Power-key polling paused
comparisons.note: Diagnostic only: this poll loop repairs a power-key IRQ issue; removal is not approved.

comparisons.label: Wi-Fi power saving
comparisons.note: Associated idle host, existing AP/channel; notification and WoWLAN tests separate.

comparisons.label: UFS runtime suspend
comparisons.note: Logger uses RAM; ordinary system background writes may still wake storage.

comparisons.label: USB development data link disabled
comparisons.note: Cable still attached; not equivalent to physically unplugged USB.

comparisons.label: USB transfer ended
comparisons.note: Whole-phone cost of a 1 MiB/s encrypted USB upload, including CPU work.

comparisons.label: Bluetooth radio off
comparisons.note: Idle radio only; no calls, audio or Bluetooth wake validation.

comparisons.label: Android forced Doze
comparisons.note: Uses existing guest network configuration; no automatic physical-host suspend.

comparisons.label: Idle Android VM shut down
comparisons.note: Host workload and Android guest workload differ by definition.

comparisons.label: Idle camera ISP runtime suspend
comparisons.note: CAMSS ISP block only; sensor capture/rails and full camera operation are not established.

remaining.S01: Stock Android and Ubuntu Touch comparisons need separately verified measurement adapters; current sweep covers host and Android/crosvm.
remaining.S03: Controller hardware sleep has no implemented independent switch; only existing touch delivery can be compared.
remaining.S06: Only s2idle is advertised. Continuous CPU sampling keeps the host awake; the driver lacks a high-resolution sleep-energy counter. A 30-minute true-suspend power average needs suitable external instrumentation. No misleading awake samples will be labeled sleep power.
remaining.S07: State propagation is a correctness issue, not an independent implemented power switch. Guest/host state snapshots are collected during Android tests.
remaining.S08: Existing sleep blocker only matches QEMU, not crosvm. New VM lifecycle/voting behavior is not implemented; testing runs under an explicit sleep inhibitor.
remaining.S09: Guest/host suspend coordination is not implemented. Idle VM overhead is measurable; coordinated suspend saving is not yet measurable.
remaining.S10: Scoped guest wake-lock bridge and VM consensus protocol remain design drafts; there is no runtime on/off option.
remaining.S11: Doze and the existing power-key polling loop are testable; broader timer batching has no implemented switch.
remaining.S12: Physical PM8xxx RTC exposes wakealarm and wake is enabled. Guest deadline aggregation is not implemented; no independent saving can yet be assigned.
remaining.S13: Runtime-PM savings can be measured; eliminating rendering work requires a separate implementation/performance decision.
remaining.S14: Native host idle power save/radio-off can be measured; WoWLAN, notification delivery, and shared/native guest networking need functional tests.
remaining.S15: GPU/UFS/CAMSS/secondary USB runtime controls are available. Sensor/camera capture, DSP/audio, interconnect and other paths need functionality and supported-control evidence.
remaining.S16: Charging limits are preserved. The charger poll interval has no runtime tuning control; charging-current samples cannot serve as discharge-power comparisons.
remaining.S17: USB data unbinding and active transfer are measurable with cable attached. Physical-unplug and charging-only cases cannot be inferred from them.
remaining.S18: Bluetooth idle radio can be compared. Modem, sensors, call/SMS and audio wake paths require working integration and event tests.
